questions.stem: The assistant panel appends tokens with setText(text + ev.text) inside a for await loop. Under a fast stream, words go missing. Why?
options: React drops state updates that arrive faster than 60 per second
The closure captures text from the render that started the loop, so every update writes stale text plus one token
for await skips iterations when the component re-renders
TextDecoder is not called with stream: true
questions.explanation: State values are snapshots per render. A long-running async loop keeps the first snapshot. Use a functional update (setText(t => t + x)) or a ref.

questions.stem: Why does the Kestrel gateway client use fetch with a stream reader instead of the browser's EventSource? Choose two.
options: EventSource only supports GET, so the prompt cannot go in a JSON body
EventSource cannot parse multi-line data fields
EventSource cannot set custom request headers such as Authorization
fetch streams are delivered in event order and EventSource ones are not
questions.explanation: EventSource is GET-only with no custom headers. It does reconnect automatically and sends Last-Event-ID, which you have to rebuild yourself with fetch.

questions.stem: A network chunk ends with \r. What must an incremental SSE parser do?
options: Treat it as a complete line ending and also dispatch the event
Process the line, but remember that a \n at the start of the next chunk belongs to this CRLF
Discard the chunk and wait for a retry
Nothing: SSE only allows LF
questions.explanation: SSE allows CRLF, LF and bare CR. A CR at a chunk boundary is ambiguous until the next chunk arrives. If you get this wrong, a CRLF split across chunks produces an empty line and dispatches an event too early.

questions.stem: The user clicks Stop while an answer streams. Which behaviours are correct? Choose two.
options: Abort the request with an AbortController so the server stops generating
Show an error alert so the user knows the answer is incomplete
Keep the partial text and mark the answer as stopped
Leave the reader open so the answer can resume later
questions.explanation: Abort to stop the generation and the cost. An abort is the user's intent, not an error, so keep what was shown and label it.

questions.stem: With React Testing Library, which query best checks that the streamed answer appears in the accessible answer region?
options: container.querySelector('.answer')
screen.getByRole('log', { name: 'Assistant answer' })
screen.getByTestId('answer')
Snapshot the whole component
questions.explanation: Query the way a user or assistive technology finds an element: by role and accessible name. Test ids and CSS selectors couple tests to implementation details.

questions.stem: Product cards in the chat should come from:
options: Regex over the model's text for SKUs and prices
Structured events (or tool results) the server emits, validated on the client
A second model call that converts the answer to JSON
Whatever the model writes inside a markdown table
questions.explanation: Render UI from structured data your services produced, not from prose the model wrote. Prices and stock shown as fact must come from the system of record.

questions.stem: TanStack Query is the right tool for which part of the storefront?
options: The token stream of the chat answer
Server state such as product lists: caching, loading and error states, refetch and invalidation
Global UI state such as whether the chat panel is open
Form validation
questions.explanation: TanStack Query manages server state. A one-off stream lives in a hook with its own lifecycle; UI state stays in components or context.

questions.stem: Which UX choices follow the human-AI interaction guidelines for a shopping assistant? Choose three.
options: Disclose that the user is talking to an AI assistant
Hide errors and show a generic answer instead
Offer a clear path to a human
Let users stop or correct the assistant
Present prices from the model as final
questions.explanation: Make clear what the system can do and how well, support efficient correction and dismissal, and offer escalation. Never present unverified model output as fact.

questions.stem: A stream ends cleanly (the reader reports done) but no done event arrived. What should the UI do?
options: Treat it as complete
Treat it as a dropped connection and offer retry
Reload the page
Hide the partial text
questions.explanation: A proxy timeout or crash can close the connection cleanly. Without the terminal event you cannot know whether the answer is complete, so say so.

questions.stem: You are asked in an interview how you use AI coding assistants on an unfamiliar repo. Which answer shows the most control?
options: I let the assistant write the feature and open the PR
I map the repo with the assistant, write a rules file, have it propose a plan, then implement in small steps with tests I review and run
I avoid assistants on unfamiliar code
I paste the whole repo into a chat
questions.explanation: Show a deliberate workflow: context first, a plan reviewed by a human, small verifiable steps, tests as the gate, and ownership of the result.

questions.stem: An async def FastAPI endpoint calls a synchronous SDK that does blocking HTTP. What happens under load?
options: FastAPI runs it in a threadpool automatically
The event loop thread is blocked for each call, so every request on that worker, health checks included, waits
Only that endpoint slows down
Python raises a RuntimeError
questions.explanation: FastAPI runs async def on the event loop. Blocking inside it stalls everything on that worker. Use def (threadpool), run_in_threadpool or an async client.

questions.stem: How do you test a FastAPI route without the real model client?
options: Monkeypatch the requests library globally
Inject the client with Depends and replace it with app.dependency_overrides in the test
Set an environment variable that disables the model
Mock the network at the OS level
questions.explanation: Dependency injection plus overrides gives deterministic tests and keeps the production wiring honest.

questions.stem: Why use keyset (cursor) pagination for product search instead of offset? Choose two.
options: Items do not repeat or disappear when rows are inserted between page requests
It allows jumping straight to page 50
Cost does not grow with the page number
It needs no ORDER BY
questions.explanation: Keyset pagination needs a stable, unique sort key, such as (price, sku). It is consistent under writes and cheap at depth. It cannot jump to an arbitrary page.

questions.stem: A reservation endpoint receives the same Idempotency-Key twice with the same body. Correct behaviour?
options: Create a second reservation
Return 409 Conflict
Return the stored response of the first request and change nothing
Return 204 No Content
questions.explanation: Idempotency makes client retries safe. Store the key with a request hash and the response. A different body under the same key is a client error.

questions.stem: Your React team hand-writes TypeScript interfaces for the catalog API, and they drift. What fixes it at the source?
options: A shared Slack channel
Export OpenAPI from FastAPI, generate the TS types (openapi-typescript), commit both, and fail CI on drift
Use any for API responses
Write JSON schema by hand
questions.explanation: Make the server's models the single source of truth and generate the client types. CI checks turn drift into a build failure.

questions.stem: Which error format is the standard choice for HTTP APIs?
options: Plain text messages
RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json)
HTML error pages
A 200 with an error field
questions.explanation: Problem details give clients a stable machine-readable type, title, status and detail. Declare them in OpenAPI so generated clients know the shape.

questions.stem: Which belong in environment configuration rather than code, following twelve-factor? Choose two.
options: Model provider API keys
The list of tool names
Database URL
The Pydantic response models
questions.explanation: Config that varies between deploys (credentials, URLs) goes in the environment. Code-level contracts stay in code.

questions.stem: When does async def genuinely help a GenAI backend?
options: CPU-heavy tokenization
Many concurrent requests that spend most of their time waiting on model and database I/O through async clients
Any endpoint, always
Only for websockets
questions.explanation: Async lets one worker hold many waiting requests. It does nothing for CPU-bound work and hurts if you call blocking code inside it.

questions.stem: You validate model output with a Pydantic model and it fails. Best next step in production?
options: Return a 500
Retry once with the validation error fed back to the model, then fall back to a safe path
Strip the invalid fields silently
Increase temperature and retry five times
questions.explanation: Treat the schema as a contract. One repair attempt with the concrete error usually works. After that, route the item to a fallback or a human instead of looping.

questions.stem: Liveness vs readiness for the catalog service: which is right?
options: Liveness should call the database and the model provider
Liveness says the process can make progress; readiness says it should receive traffic and may check dependencies
Both should return 200 always
Readiness should restart the pod
questions.explanation: A liveness probe that depends on downstreams turns a dependency blip into a restart storm.

questions.stem: A client timeout is 10 s, but long answers take 14 s, and the client retries on timeout. What does this cost?
options: Nothing, timed-out requests are not billed
Each retry is a full generation that the provider completes and bills, so one question can cost several answers
Only input tokens are billed twice
The provider cancels the first request automatically
questions.explanation: The server keeps generating after the client gives up. Size timeouts to the output budget or stream, retry only what is retryable, and cap attempts across fallbacks.

questions.stem: Which errors should an LLM gateway retry with backoff? Choose two.
options: 429 rate limited (honour retry-after)
400 invalid request (prompt too long)
529 / 503 overloaded
401 unauthorized
questions.explanation: Retry transient capacity errors with exponential backoff and jitter. Client errors will fail the same way every time.

questions.stem: Where must the rule 'a return needs the customer's confirmation' be enforced?
options: In the system prompt
In the tool description
In code: the write tool only creates a pending action that a separate confirm call executes
In the model's fine-tuning
questions.explanation: Instructions are guidance; the model can be steered or can make mistakes. Enforce controls in the code paths the model cannot reach.

questions.stem: The order tool should behave how when a customer asks about someone else's order id?
options: Return the order but hide the name
Return the same error as for a missing order
Return 'access denied: belongs to another customer'
Ask the model to decide
questions.explanation: The agent acts with the caller's permissions. The same response for 'not yours' and 'missing' leaks nothing.

questions.stem: How should prompt layout look for good prompt caching?
options: Dynamic data first, static instructions last
Static system prompt and tool definitions first, cache breakpoint, then per-request data
Put the current timestamp at the top so the cache stays fresh
Caching is automatic regardless of order
questions.explanation: The cache matches a byte-identical prefix. Anything that changes per request must come after the breakpoint.

questions.stem: A tool fails with a backend 503. What goes back to the model?
options: Nothing; abort the request
A tool_result with is_error true and an actionable message
A fake successful result
The full stack trace
questions.explanation: Structured errors let the model recover or apologise. Stack traces waste context and can leak internals.

questions.stem: Which measures belong in a per-request cost and latency budget? Choose three.
options: Input, output and cache tokens per call
Time to first token
Number of attempts including discarded ones
The model's temperature
Lines of code in the service
questions.explanation: Log tokens and cost per attempt, including retries you threw away, plus user-visible latency. OTel GenAI conventions name these attributes.

questions.stem: Product answers sometimes invent prices. Which mitigations are most effective? Choose two.
options: Ground answers on tool results and render prices from structured data
Raise max_tokens
Allow the assistant to say it does not know
Ask the model to be accurate
questions.explanation: Grounding plus a permitted 'I don't know' reduces hallucination. Prices shown to customers should come from the catalog, not from generated text.

questions.stem: Where does a fallback model belong?
options: Hard-coded at every call site
Behind a small gateway interface with a total attempt budget across primary and fallback
In the front end
Nowhere: fallbacks are never worth it
questions.explanation: Centralise retry, fallback and budget logic, so one bug does not multiply calls and behaviour can be tested with fakes.

questions.stem: An agent loop has no turn limit and a tool that keeps returning 'try again'. What is the minimum fix?
options: Lower temperature
A max-turns limit with a graceful handoff message and an audit entry
A longer system prompt
Retry the whole request
questions.explanation: Bound every loop. A clear stop condition plus a human path beats an endless tool-calling spiral that burns tokens.
